title: [recoverability] spawn reads a database password from a passfile (PGPASSFILE, else ~/.pgpass), as libpq does, when the URL holds none; inert on a host whose URLs hold their passwords (part 1 of A1)
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 109 [recoverability] (part 1 of A1, inert until 110 uses it): spawn reads a database password from a passfile, as libpq does, when the URL holds none.

Read crates/spawn-postgres/src/lib.rs (PostgresStore::connect, connect_with_statement_timeout, connect_in_schema, maintenance_config and every other place a postgres::Config is parsed from a URL), host.rs (cluster_identity) and wake.rs.

Why (sync/url-leak-sources.md; the lead and the owner, 11-13). An engine's environment holds SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL with its password, and the supervisor's holds a live login with its password, so any print of the environment puts a password into a transcript. The fix at the source (objectives 110 and 111) hands engines URLs that hold no password, with the password in a 0600 passfile that the engines' deny list covers. psql already reads such a file (PGPASSFILE, else ~/.pgpass). spawn and its tests do not: given a URL without a password, they fail to log in. This objective gives spawn the same fallback. It changes nothing for a URL that holds a password, so it is inert until 110.

Required behaviour, for every connection spawn makes from a URL (the store, the dashboard's reader, the schema per test and its drop, the maintenance and identity reads):
- When the URL holds no password, the password is the first matching line of the passfile: PGPASSFILE when set, else $HOME/.pgpass. A line is `host:port:database:user:password`. `*` in any of the first four fields matches anything, and `\:` and `\\` stand for `:` and `\`. Lines starting with `#` are comments. Matching is as libpq does it: host is the URL's TCP host by name, or a socket directory by its path, and `localhost` also matches a connection over the default socket directory; port is the URL's port (default 5432); database and user are the URL's (the user defaulting as the postgres crate defaults it).
- A passfile that its group or others can read or write is not used: spawn says once on stderr "spawn: passfile <path> has group or world access; not used (chmod 600)", and connects without a password. That is libpq's rule; libpq's message differs.
- No line matches, the file is missing, or the URL holds a password: as today. A URL with an empty password (`user:@host`) holds one here, the empty one; libpq would read the passfile. Nothing writes such URLs. The URL's own password always wins, as with libpq.
- The password is never printed: not in an error, not in a log line, not in Debug output. A refused passfile is named by its path, never by a value.
- The owner's password from the passfile is the owner's password: the restricted logins (spawn_supervisor, spawn_reader, spawn_human), whose passwords derive from it (role_url, and the migration that sets them), work the same when it comes from the passfile.

Inert on a host whose URLs hold their passwords. With a password in the URL, the lookup returns before reading anything (one Option check), so nothing changes, not even the timing of the first connect. A URL without a password, which fails to log in today against a server that asks for one, now reads PGPASSFILE or ~/.pgpass: one stat of a missing file costs microseconds, and one small read when the file is there.

The owner password rotated (for the rotation runbook): the derived logins' passwords are PBKDF2 of the owner's password, salted, and the migration (`spawn init-db`, also run by deploy) sets them. After the owner's password changes, whether in the URL or in the passfile, role_url derives the new passwords at once. The database keeps the old ones until `spawn init-db` runs again, so until then serve's reads (spawn_reader), the supervisor's login and spawn_human fail to log in ("database unreachable"), while the owner's own connections work. Run `spawn init-db` right after a rotation. This objective does not change that: it is today's behaviour, wherever the password comes from.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-postgres/src/passfile.rs (new: the lookup), crates/spawn-postgres/src/lib.rs (the lookup used wherever a Config is made from a URL to connect: connect, connect_with_statement_timeout, the maintenance read, role_url, url_password, cluster_identity, the test database probe), host.rs (test_database_read), wake.rs (listen) and testing.rs (TestSchema's drop and its tests' own connections, so a test schema under a password-less URL is dropped as it is made). One crate, about 230 lines with its unit tests.

Also, doc lines only, made by the lead in his own commit (not this objective's): the short live password in three example lines becomes a placeholder: crates/spawn-postgres/tests/api.rs line 5 (a doc comment), docs/architecture.md line 121, and scripts/blackbox/run-scenarios.sh line 7 (a comment). This objective does not touch tests/api.rs.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/109.sh. The scenario makes its own login with a made-up password and its own database on the server of SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL. If that server lets the login in with no password, the scenario cannot judge (exit 2). URLs below name that login with no password; the scenario's HOME is its own.
(1) With PGPASSFILE a 0600 file holding a matching line, after a comment line and a line for another user, `spawn init-db` exits 0, and `spawn serve`'s GET /api/fleet answers 200.
(2) The same with a line whose password holds `:` and `\`, written escaped (`\:` and `\\`), and the login's password set to match: exit 0.
(3) With no PGPASSFILE, the line in $HOME/.pgpass (0600): exit 0.
(4) With neither, `spawn init-db` exits non-zero with an authentication error.
(5) With PGPASSFILE mode 0644: exits non-zero, and stderr names the file with "group or world access; not used".
(6) With the URL holding a wrong password and the passfile the right one: exits non-zero (the URL wins).
(7) Nothing spawn wrote in (1) to (6) holds the made-up password.
check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass.
